diagnosis.bottleneck: The LEFT_DELIM_JOIN (node 5) probes a 312K-row inner hash join (nodes 7-9) for each of the 265 zones, where the inner side scans the full trips table (495K rows) and builds a hash on the correlated join key.

hypotheses.claim: NOT IN over a subquery forces a null-aware anti join, which is expensive. (matched: not in (select t.ratecodeid from lake.trips t where t.pulocationid = z.locationid) order b)

The LEFT_DELIM_JOIN implements a correlated NOT IN with a nullable RatecodeID, forcing a per-row probe of the large inner hash join; rewriting to NOT EXISTS with an explicit IS NOT NULL guard or a LEFT JOIN … IS NULL allows a single anti-join instead of repeated probing.

The inner HASH_JOIN (node 7) builds its hash table from a full scan of trips (495K rows) even though the correlated predicate restricts it to the current zone; the planner cannot push the correlation inside, so the hash table is rebuilt or probed for every outer row.
The SEQ_SCAN on trips (node 8) reads all 495K rows and both columns without partition pruning or predicate push-down, so the scan cost dominates the inner join build time for every probe.
